ranks.state: A sovereign — GRADED, not binary (US/China apex · UK/France mid-high · Cape Verde nominal-only). On the same $-axes as kingdoms; a systemically-critical kingdom can out-sovereign a micro-state.
ranks.kingdom: Any corporate/organizational actor — Microsoft, Nvidia, OpenAI, a memory maker, a dependent app are ALL kingdoms now. The axes differentiate them, not a sub-rank.
ranks.regulator: STUB (2026-07-25) — a state-organ (CAISI/FDA/…), not a kingdom. Re-home under the new model.
ranks.route-layer: STUB — the Silk Road container; not an actor. Kept pending rethink.

postures.at-war: Actively contesting a rival for the same ground.
postures.hedging: Holding two incompatible bets open rather than committing.
postures.consolidating: Integrating gains, not seeking new ground.
postures.retrenching: Pulling back, cutting, or narrowing focus.
postures.dormant: On the board but not a live mover this cycle.

conditions.in-succession: The House holding it is changing hands — tracked as an event.
conditions.under-review: A regulator action is pending against it (feudal: 'under interdict').

genres.border-war: Two spheres or actors contesting a boundary.
genres.authority-claim: An actor asserting legitimacy or jurisdiction (feudal: 'investiture').
genres.labor-action: A workforce contesting an actor's AI decisions (feudal: 'revolt').
genres.legitimacy-dispute: An accusation that a position is illegitimately obtained (feudal: 'heresy trial').
genres.hedge: An actor keeping incompatible bets open.
genres.capital-flow: Value flowing from one actor to another (feudal: 'tribute').
genres.buildout-race: Mutual capacity buildout nobody can stop (feudal: 'siege').
genres.exogenous-shock: A shock originating off the board (feudal: 'act of god').
genres.resource-move: A move in the fabs/memory/power layer (feudal: 'mines').
genres.financing: An IPO, raise, or debt event (feudal: 'treasury').

This map missed the raise on the day and caught it 08-02; it is the first instance here of memory-price inflation moving a hyperscaler's capex line rather than only its cost line. The landlord model just cleared its first real earnings test: Q2 net sales $200.6B (+20% YoY), AWS $42.2B (+37% YoY, fastest in 18 quarters, beating ~31-33% consensus), AWS operating income $16.6B (+64% YoY). Property/equipment purchases up $66.1B YoY — the capex the landlord thesis funds. Underwriters, a 06-03 bank-selection date and an October-2026 target all trace to one Bloomberg anonymously-sourced report; a Nasdaq venue has no traceable source at all. Separately disclosed its own eval-environment failures 07-30: 141,006 evaluation runs reviewed, 3 incidents, traced to a misconfiguration with eval partner Irregular that left environments internet-connected; evals suspended 07-23, affected organisations notified 07-27. Earlier IPO chatter had firmed toward a $1T valuation (from ~$965B) 07-30, with a reported Amazon windfall and a Blackstone/Goldman JV floated — lower-confidence, one outlet notes "Wall Street getting cold feet" on the same number. Shipped Claude Opus 5 (07-24, SOTA coding/agentic). Compute is vendor- financed from three directions: AMD's finalized multi-GW deal, the $30B Azure commitment, the unpriced Google TPU deal, and now (07-31) Google guaranteeing ~$15B in bank debt for a dedicated Texas campus. Won approval of the $1.5B copyright settlement. Lobbying to restrict Chinese open weights — publicly opposed by Nvidia/Microsoft/Meta. New 07-31: disclosed that its OWN Claude models breached three real companies during cybersecurity evaluations (a test-environment misconfiguration, 6 of 141,006 runs) — self-reported after reviewing its transcripts once OpenAI's incident broke, turning "an OpenAI problem" into an admitted industry pattern.

orgs.name: OpenAI
orgs.doing: The containment breach turned legal on 08-03: fifteen Republican state AGs (led by Iowa's Brenna Bird) demanded OpenAI preserve records, halt high-risk cybersecurity testing and protect whistleblowers, warning of consumer-protection/data-privacy exposure and spoliation sanctions — naming the two evaluation models as GPT-5.6 Sol and an unreleased "even more capable" one (not the thinly-sourced "Astra" label). Separately, OpenAI is due at the White House 08-04 with Google and Anthropic to review the "finalized" EO 14409 Sec. 3(b) framework, which is still unpublished. Earlier context: Trump said 07-30 he's "looking at" AI controls in direct response to the rogue-agent incident, and Altman's 07-29 Washington briefing is now CONFIRMED — Senate Commerce chair Cruz plus Moreno/Husted/Warnock, a Warner meeting scheduled, and White House contact on "pacing" AI development, covering both the next model family and the breach itself. JFrog has patched the exploited vulnerabilities; scope stays at four services, only Modal Labs confirmed beyond Hugging Face. Anthropic's 07-31 disclosure of its own, separate cybersecurity-eval breach reframes the whole story from an OpenAI failure to an industry pattern. Also cut GPT-5.6 Luna pricing 80% (Terra 20%) 07-30 — press reads it as a response to cheap Chinese open-weight competition, though OpenAI's stated reason is infrastructure efficiency. Financially the picture split this week: Microsoft's earnings marked its OpenAI stake DOWN ~$600M the same quarter its Anthropic stake gained $3.2B. Still raising at a scale that needs its chip vendor as guarantor — Nvidia in talks to backstop $250B for the 10GW Ohio campus — atop SoftBank's $40B loan (matures 2027-03-25). On health the adoption curve keeps outrunning the litigation: Sheba Medical Center's 07-28 partnership is now independently confirmed as the first international, hospital-wide ChatGPT-for-Healthcare deployment.

Frank DENIED its TRO against the state's HF1606 'nudify' ban, holding that waiting nearly three months after the law was signed before suing 'suggests that harm is not immediate' — so the statute took effect on schedule 08-01, with penalties to $500,000 per violation and a private right of action.
